## Package version handling (`[tool.setuptools_scm]`) {#sec-ch11-version}

### Summary

The kintera version is not written in any source file. It is derived from git tags when the package is built, and
installed as package metadata, which `kintera.__version__` then reports. A source tree without usable git
metadata, such as a release tarball made by an old git, would otherwise report `0.0`. A downstream package that
requires a minimum kintera version would then refuse it. A *release floor* removes that failure: such a tree
reports at least the floor version recorded in the build configuration.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Give every build a version that is never below its last release.

**Data.** Git tags `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>`; `fallback_version` in the build configuration.

**Placement.** At build or install time (setuptools_scm); read back on `import kintera`.

**Activation.** Always; `version_scheme` names the floored scheme.

**Guarantee / limits.** No usable tag gives at least the floor; a real tag gives its own version.

**Evidence.** `test_version_floor.py`, `test_version_fallback.py`; see the Tests layer.
:::

### Derivation

No derivation: this scheme reads metadata.

### Numerical method

No numerical method and no figure. `floored_guess_next_dev`
({{< code scm_version_scheme.py floored_guess_next_dev >}}) decides the version in these steps:

1. With no `fallback_version` configured, use setuptools_scm's `guess-next-dev` scheme.
2. If the tag found is a real tag (its release is not the no-tag value `0.0`), or is at or above the floor, use
   `guess-next-dev`. A tree whose newest reachable tag is below the floor keeps its own version.
3. Otherwise (no usable tag) return the floor. When the version is exact and knows its commit, append the commit
   as a local segment, `<floor>+g<commit>`, so the result stays apart from the release itself.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| version scheme | {{< code scm_version_scheme.py floored_guess_next_dev >}} | `floored_guess_next_dev` | `version_scheme` |
| floor and scheme | {{< code pyproject.toml >}} | `[tool.setuptools_scm]` | always |
| runtime version | {{< code python/__init__.py >}} | `__version__` | on import |

: Code map of version handling. {#tbl-ch11-version-code}

The build configuration {{< code pyproject.toml >}} declares the version `dynamic`, sets
`fallback_version = "2.5.13"`, and names the scheme as `scm_version_scheme:floored_guess_next_dev`, so the floor
applies to `pip install`, `python -m build` and `python -m setuptools_scm` alike. Its comment says the floor is
raised when a downstream minimum needs it, not at every release. At run time `__version__` is read from the
installed metadata with `importlib.metadata.version("kintera")`, and is `0.0.0` when no metadata is found
({{< code python/__init__.py >}}).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_version_floor.py` | the floor is not newer than the newest `v*` tag | exact | version comparison |
| `test_version_floor.py` | old-git and tagless archives report at least the floor, with the commit | exact | version comparison |
| `test_version_floor.py` | a plain copy reports the floor; a tree tagged below it keeps its own version | exact | version comparison |
| `test_version_fallback.py` | a `git archive` of the checkout reports at least the newest tag | exact | version comparison |

: Tests of version handling. {#tbl-ch11-version-tests}

The cases export the checkout with `git archive`, rewrite its `.git_archival.txt` into the form an old or tagless
git leaves, and run `python -m setuptools_scm` on the tree ({{< code tests/test_version_floor.py scm_version >}}).
Further cases cover a real `v0.0.0` tag and the checkout's own tags
({{< code tests/test_version_floor.py test_clone_tagged_v0_0_0_reports_its_own_version >}},
{{< code tests/test_version_floor.py test_this_checkout_is_versioned_from_its_own_tags >}}). The cases skip when
setuptools_scm is not installed, when git fails, or (fallback test) when no release tag is reachable, as in a
shallow clone without tags. This draft has not run them (missing evidence).

### Limits

- `kintera.__version__` reports `0.0.0` for an import from a tree that was never installed; the floor does not
  apply there (read from {{< code python/__init__.py >}}; not tested).
- The floor is maintained by hand; only the test that it is not ahead of the newest tag guards it.
